title: Impact of SEM Parameters on Electron Beam-Induced Heating: Experimental and Simulation Insights
content: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) enables high-resolution imaging and crystallographic analysis by techniques such as electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). However, prolonged electron beam exposure can lead to localized heating, which might affect sample integrity and properties and, therefore, compromises the measurement accuracy of EBSD [1,2]. This effect is particularly relevant in experiments involving long electron beam exposures on temperature-sensitive materials or in in-situ heating experiments, as uncontrolled temperature fluctuations could cause unintended structural changes.
